Dying middle class is misleading. The size of the upper class has expanded, which accounts for a good chunk of the shrinkage - the middle class moved up.

The notion that the middle class is shrinking is controversial because the economic boundaries that define the middle class vary. In 2006 households that earn between $25,000 and $75,000 represent approximately the middle half of the income distribution tables provided by the U.S. Census Bureau.

Keep in mind these are HOUSEHOLDS. $75k for a family of 4 is living in a crappy area of town off of rice and beans most the time for most areas. I don't even want to think about $25k for the same situation. More or less "middle class" no longer refers to a situation where a family can live modest but incredibly comfortably ("Sure, we can go to TGIF for dinner!"). Middle class now refers to an income category where families struggle ("We're going to Taco Bell, and everyone can only get one item from the dollar menu!").

If you use better ranges (25k - 75k is terrible as you pointed out), the news is positive:
http://www.cato.org/blog/middle-class-shrinks-number-high-income-households-grows

One of the most eye opening is the last graph about hourly wages (which typically makes up a large portion of what many consider the mid to lower middle class).
